```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## Variables of interest

- **Genes:** *PTX3* (from Submission 1), *CXCR2*, and *RUNDC3A*
- **Continuous covariate:** maternal baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D (ng/mL)
- **Categorical covariate 1:** pregnancy outcome (Normal vs Preeclampsia)
- **Categorical covariate 2 (derived from continuous):** vitamin D status
  (Deficient < 20, Insufficient 20-29.9, Sufficient 30+ ng/mL)

```{r packages}
# load needed library
library(tidyverse)
```

## 1. Load the raw files

```{r load}
covar     <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
expr      <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
geneNames <- read_csv("data/GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```

## 2. Clean the covariate data (same steps as Submission 1)

Each covariate value is stored as text such as `"bmi_kg/m2: 37.52"`, so keep only the part after `": "` and convert numbers to numeric.

```{r clean-covar, results = "hide"}
covar_clean <- covar |> 
  # Rename first column name by position
  rename(subjectID = 1) |> 
  # For every column except the IDs, keep only the text after ": "; consulted
  # the help of Claude for this step to help with str_removal, detecting patterns
  mutate(across(-c(subjectID, geoID),
                ~ str_remove(.x, "^.*: "))) |> 
  # Convert the continuous variables from text to numeric
  mutate(across(c(mat_age_yrs, 
                  delivery_gestAge_wks, 
                  sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                  mat_BMI, 
                  mat_vitD), 
                as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(
    # Pregnancy outcome as a factor, with normal and preeclampsia levels
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia, 
                               levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
    # Turn asthma into a labeled factor, either 0 or 1
    mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, 
                        levels = c("0", "1"), 
                        labels = c("Healthy", "Asthma")),
    # convert to factor variable
    batch_Microarray = factor(batch_Microarray),
    # turn continuous mat_vitD to categorical vitD_status variable
    # chose the intervals and cutoffs based off of existing clinical studies
    # and standard medical practices
    vitD_status = cut(mat_vitD,
                      breaks = c(-Inf, 20, 30, Inf),
                      right  = FALSE,   
                      labels = c("Deficient (<20)", 
                                 "Insufficient (20-29.9)", 
                                 "Sufficient (30+)"))
  )

summary(covar_clean)
count(covar_clean, preg_preeclampsia, vitD_status)
```

## 3. Build a long data frame with all of the genes

Building a data frame that holds every gene, because the function needs a data frame, so it can pull out whichever genes it is given.

```{r long-data, results = "hide"}
expr_long <- expr |> 
  # Probe ID column has no header; name it so it can be joined
  rename(PROBEID = 1) |> 
  # Attach gene names from the linker file
  left_join(geneNames, by = "PROBEID") |> 
  # convert to long format, so one row per gene per sample
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("GSM"),
               names_to  = "geoID",
               values_to = "expression")

# double check that every probe has a gene name, and no gene appears twice
sum(is.na(expr_long$GENE))
expr_long |>  
  distinct(PROBEID, GENE) |>  
  count(GENE) |>  
  filter(n > 1)  |>  
  nrow()
```

## 4. Merge with covariates and verify the match
```{r merge, results = "hide"}
# check if set of sample IDs in both files?
setequal(unique(expr_long$geoID), covar_clean$geoID)

analysis_long <- covar_clean |> 
  inner_join(expr_long, by = "geoID")

# Expect 157 samples x 500 genes = 78,500 rows, with 157 unique samples
# passed the check
nrow(analysis_long)
n_distinct(analysis_long$geoID)

# Check if merged PTX3 value for one sample equals the raw file value
analysis_long |> 
  filter(geoID == "GSM2264346", GENE == "PTX3")  |> 
  pull(expression)

expr |>  
  rename(PROBEID = 1)  |>  
  filter(PROBEID == 8083594)  |>  
  pull(GSM2264346)
```

## 5. Shared plot theme and colors (same from Submission 1)

```{r theme, results = "hide"}
# One theme for consistency across all plots; publication quality
theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# shared colors
outcome_colors <- c("Normal" = "#4C72B0", "Preeclampsia" = "#C44E52")
```

## 6. Plotting function

plot_genes() function takes the following inputs: a data frame and a vector of one or more gene names. For each gene it loops through, it makes the three Submission 1 plots (histogram, scatterplot vs vitamin D, boxplot by vitamin D status and outcome) and prints them, optionally saves them, and returns them in a named list.

```{r function}
# takes the input of a data frame, a vector of genes, into the figures directory
plot_genes <- function(df, genes, save = FALSE, out_dir = "figures") {

  # First initialize an empty list
  all_plots <- list()

  # Loop through each gene provided and produce the plots (huge for loop!)
  for (gene in genes) {
    
    # Keep only this gene's rows (one row per sample)
    # rename input data frame as gene_df
    gene_df <- df |>  
      filter(GENE == gene)
    # Axis label reused by all three plots
    y_lab <- paste(gene, "expression (log2 intensity)")
    
    # Plot 1: histogram showing distribution of expression; essentially same
    # code as submission 1
    p_hist <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = expression)) +
      # 0.05-wide bins suit the narrow range of log2 expression values
      geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "#3A7D7C", color = "white",
                     linewidth = 0.3) +
      # Dashed line at the median as a reference point
      geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median(expression)),
                 linetype = "dashed", color = "#1F2A37", linewidth = 0.6) +
      # Bars sit directly on the x-axis, with some space on top
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
      labs(title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Expression"),
           x = y_lab,
           y = "Number of samples",
           caption = paste0("Dashed line = median; n = ", nrow(gene_df))) +
      theme_pub

    # Once again same thing but for plot 2: scatterplot of vitamin D 
    # vs expression. same code as submission 1, just changing the inputs.
    p_scatter <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = expression)) +
      # One point per woman, colored by outcome
      geom_point(aes(color = preg_preeclampsia), alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
      # Overall linear trend with 95% confidence band
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = TRUE) +
      scale_color_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
      labs(title = paste("Maternal Vitamin D vs", gene, "Expression"),
           x = "Maternal 25(OH)D at baseline (ng/mL)",
           y = y_lab,
           color = "Pregnancy outcome") +
      theme_pub

    # Same thing again, but for plot 3: boxplot by both categorical variables
    p_box <- ggplot(gene_df, aes(x = vitD_status, y = expression,
                                 fill = preg_preeclampsia)) +
      # Boxes side by side for each outcome; hide outliers because
      # all points are drawn below
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
      # Individual women, jittered sideways and aligned with their box
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,
                                                 dodge.width  = 0.8),
                 size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
      # edit in that particular looped gene
      labs(title = paste(gene, "Expression by Vitamin D Status and Outcome"),
           x = "Maternal vitamin D status (ng/mL)",
           y = y_lab,
           fill = "Pregnancy outcome") +
      theme_pub

    # Print all three plots so they appear in the knitted document
    print(p_hist)
    print(p_scatter)
    print(p_box)

    # Save the plots named by gene if save is set to TRUE, the default input
    # is that save is set as FALSE initially; this is optional, that way doesn't
    # continuously rewrite plots each time functino is run
    if (save) {
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("histogram_", gene, ".png")),
             p_hist, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("scatter_vitD_", gene, ".png")),
             p_scatter, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)
      ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0("boxplot_vitD_outcome_", gene, ".png")),
             p_box, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
    }

    # Store this gene's plots in the list under the gene's name
    # This way when the loop finishes you can pull out any single plot later
    # without rerunning the function
    all_plots[[gene]] <- list(histogram = p_hist,
                              scatter   = p_scatter,
                              boxplot   = p_box)
  }
}
```

## 7. Run the function on three genes

```{r run-function, fig.height = 5}
# interested genes in the list
genes_of_interest <- c("PTX3", "CXCR2", "RUNDC3A")

# Set save = TRUE to save the 9 figures in figures folder
# Set save = FALSE in final pdf/markdown because don't want to keep running
# this over and over

# takes the analysis_long data frame input created from step 3 and 4 as input
# also takes list genes in previous line as input
gene_plots <- plot_genes(analysis_long, genes_of_interest, save = FALSE)
```
